options: A regulator announcing the official price of a security each morning
The process by which a market price emerges from the interaction of buy and sell orders
The process of discovering which company issued a given stock
A method for predicting future prices using historical data
questions.explain: Price discovery describes how a market's price emerges from the ongoing interaction of buy and sell orders, not from any single party's decision.

questions.q: A market maker who just bought a large block of shares from one client, and now worries the price could fall before finding a buyer, is most directly facing which component of the bid-ask spread?
options: Order-processing cost
Inventory risk
Adverse selection
Tick size
questions.explain: Inventory risk is the risk of holding a position between trades — exactly the exposure a market maker takes on after buying shares before offloading them.

questions.q: Why does adverse selection widen the bid-ask spread?
options: Because exchanges charge higher fees to informed traders
Because market makers lose money systematically when trading against better-informed counterparties, so that risk gets priced in
Because adverse selection only affects bond markets, not equities
Because it reduces the operational cost of processing trades
questions.explain: If informed traders are more likely to trade right before news moves the price, the market maker on the other side loses money on average — so the spread compensates for that risk.

options: The maximum number of shares in one order
The smallest allowed increment between prices, putting a floor on how narrow a spread can be
The exact time of day the market opens
Which asset class a security belongs to
questions.explain: Tick size is the smallest allowed price increment. A market maker cannot quote a spread narrower than one tick.

questions.q: How does an opening or closing auction differ from continuous trading?
options: It matches orders one at a time, the instant they cross, just like continuous trading
Orders accumulate without executing, then all crossing orders are matched simultaneously at one single computed price
It only allows limit orders, never market orders
It is used exclusively in bond markets, never in equities
questions.explain: In an auction, orders submitted beforehand don't execute immediately — the exchange instead computes one price that matches the maximum volume and executes everything at that price at once.
